# who-may-call

**Replaces:** `generated/server/main.ts` entirely, with `main.ts` here. It is the generated main.ts with every route kept (all of the merged acme's operations) and one change, marked `// PLANTED:`. A handler cannot plant this by itself, because the runtime's wrapper (`Handlers.serve`) checks the declaration's `allowed` before any handler runs; the break has to be in the gate.
**Breaks:** the server serves `allowance.grant` with a declaration whose `allowed` lets anyone call: `operation: { ...allowanceGrant.declaration, allowed: [Blueprint.anyone] }`. The wrapper then lets every principal through, so bob reaches the handler. The only other differences from the generated file are the header comment and the `Blueprint` import. The builder should regenerate this fixture from whatever `generated/server/main.ts` the generator emits then, changing only that gate line.
**Eval that must fail:** 5, who may call. The eval decides who lacks the role from the world's facts (organization owner = ada's person) and the declaration's `allowed`, never from what the server did.
**Failure shape:** `allowance.grant who may call ✘ grant-an-allowance "bob is refused and the handler never runs": caller bob (person per_...) lacks owner of organization org_..., and was answered, not refused`. Other evals and journey steps may fail too, since bob's call now succeeds and writes an allowance.
